label: Flooded area (monthly, Sentinel-1 SAR) — trend 2018→year (Sen's slope)
colormap: continuous red -> white -> green (red = low / decrease, white = middle / no change, green = high / increase); symmetric about 0, fixed across years
scale: linear, symmetric about 0 (fixed across years: 98th percentile of |slope|)
native_resolution: 10 m Sentinel-1 RTC read at 160 m, classified on a 0.004 deg (~440 m) grid
source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 IW GRD RTC (sentinel-1-rtc) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
basis: wet-season (Jun-Sep) mean flooded fraction (%) of the known area of each 0.02° cell from the monthly Sentinel-1 classification (gap-filled as in flood_s1_pipeline; class 'flooded' only, permanent open water excluded, as in the county series flood_s1_flood_pct). Missing months are filled by the climatology-anomaly method (yearly = mean monthly climatology + mean anomaly of the observed months); a year needs >= half of the season observed unless stated otherwise.
notes: Each image = per-pixel Theil-Sen (Sen's) slope of the yearly values from 2018 through the image year (>= 3 years), in percentage points/yr. Continuous colour: red = decrease, white = no change, green = increase (bilinear smoothing between cells; black hatching = data but too few years for a slope). No significance test is applied per pixel: with 3-8 yearly points a slope is a description of change, not proof of a trend.
